title: Leaving for work
byline: On Monday, April 20, at 6:27 AM, the auspicious departure for work begins with traditional observances meant to bring prosperity and success.

title: NIC one-oay service resumes as system restored from today.
byline: The Department of Registration of Persons has announced that all public services, including the one-day service for issuing National Identity Cards (NICs), will resume from today (20).

title: Will Kumara Jayakody’s resignation trigger a Cabinet reshuffle?
byline: A Cabinet reshuffle becomes inevitable if President Anura Kumara Dissanayake picks someone from the current board of Ministers to fill the Energy Ministry portfolio that fell vacant after the resignation of Kumara Jayakody from the post.

title: Oil prices rise after Trump says Iranian ship seized
byline: Global oil prices rose in Monday morning trade in Asia after President Donald Trump said the US has intercepted and seized an Iran-flagged cargo ship.

title: Project complex with significant financial outlays - Indian Foreign Secretary
byline: Asserting that there is no further time to lose on strategic projects such as the Trincomalee energy hub, Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said yesterday that although a timeline has not yet been established, discussions are in progress, given the complexity of the project and its significant financial outlays.

title: Kumara Jayakody - A man who faces the test of time
byline: Days after Kumara Jayakody resigned as the Energy Minister making him the first minister to step down amidst corruption allegations in the NPP government, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake will this week appoint an already existing cabinet minister to the post to temporarily look into the affairs of the ministry, the Daily Mirror learns.

title: US energy chief says gas prices could stay above $3 per gallon until next year
byline: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Sunday he believes gas prices have peaked but predicted that they may stay above $3 per gallon ​until next year.

title: Louisiana man kills 7 of his children, another child in mass shooting
byline: A gunman in the southern US state of Louisiana killed eight children, including seven of his own, and shot two other people before being killed by police, authorities have said.

title: ‘We are not afraid of war’: Iranians rally in support of government
byline: Thousands of people have taken to the streets of Tehran in support of Iran’s government, with some voicing a “complete distrust” towards the US and urging Iranian officials not to back down.

title: US intercepts and seizes Iranian-flagged cargo ship, Trump says
byline: The US has intercepted an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf as part of its naval blockade, Donald Trump has said.

title: India extends OCI eligibility to sixth generation of Indian-origin Sri Lankans
byline: In what appears to be a major bonanza for Sri Lankan Tamils of Indian origin, India has extended eligibility for the Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) card to the fifth and sixth generations.

title: Tourism earnings plunge to five-month low as the Middle East conflict derails targets
byline: Sri Lanka’s foreign exchange earnings from tourism suffered a severe blow in March 2026, plummeting 37 percent year-on-year to US$ 223.7 million.

title: March remittances hit four-month high on seasonal inflows
byline: ​Sri Lanka’s worker remittances rose sharply in March, supported by seasonal inflows ahead of key festival periods, with receipts climbing to their highest level in four months, Central Bank data showed.

title: Sri Lanka secures continued IMF backing at 2026 Spring Meetings
byline: ​A Sri Lankan delegation led by Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe has held productive discussions with the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and investors during the 2026 Spring Meetings.

title: Severe lightning and thundershowers expected after 1.00 p.m. – Met Department
byline: The Meteorology Department has warned that thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely to occur in most parts of the island after 1.00 p.m. today.

title: Uncertain of joint opposition May Day rally: Sujeewa
byline: Responding to speculation on a joint May Day rally by some parties in the Opposition, Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP Sujeewa Senasinghe said today that it is not possible to come up with a definite word about it.

title: Delay in coal environmental report “suspicious” – Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa
byline: The Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights has raised concerns over the delayed publication of an environmental impact assessment related to recently imported substandard coal shipments to Sri Lanka.

title: Tehran vows swift response after US seizes Iranian-flagged vessel
byline: The US says it has attacked and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel it said had tried to evade its naval blockade near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. Tehran’s joint military command vowed to respond, throwing the fate of a fragile ceasefire into question days before it expires.

title: Harsha defends HSBC CEO’s comment on Sri Lanka’s oil purchase
byline: Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP Harsha de Silva yesterday referred to Daily Mirror report published under the title ’CPC rejects US dollars 286 per barrel claim, threatens legal action’’ and alleged that there has been an attempt to manipulate the statement made by the HSBC CEO.

title: Indian Vice President visits Nuwara Eliya to inspect housing project
byline: Indian Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan arrived in Nuwara Eliya this morning (20) to inspect the progress of the Indian-funded housing project for the Indian-origin Tamil community.

title: Island-wide police sweep nets over 600 suspects; 98 arrested on open warrants
byline: Sri Lanka Police have arrested 98 individuals with open warrants during a series of special island-wide crime prevention and anti-narcotics operations conducted across all police divisions.

title: Two foreign journalists nabbed at BIA with ‘Kush’ worth Rs. 64 mn
byline: Two foreign social media journalists were arrested this morning (20) by officers of the Airport Police Narcotics Bureau for attempting to smuggle a stock of “Kush” drugs valued at over Rs. 64 million.

title: Low-floor priority bus service for persons with disabilities to begin tomorrow
byline: A low-floor priority bus service for persons with disabilities will commence tomorrow (21) from the Makumbura Multimodal Center (MMC), the Transport, Highways and Urban Development Ministry said.

title: Expressways generate Rs. 48.5 mn in 24 hours; nearly Rs. 490 mn earned over 10 days
byline: Traffic on the expressways (E01, E02, E03 and E04) generated a total revenue of Rs. 48,500,040 during the 24-hour period from midnight on April 19 to midnight on April 20, 2026, according to an official traffic summary.

title: GMOA comes under criticism from rank and file
byline: The recent strike launched by the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has come under criticism, with sources claiming it was poorly organized and failed to pressure the Government.

title: NIC one-day service resumes as system restored from today.
byline: The Department of Registration of Persons has announced that all public services, including the one-day service for issuing National Identity Cards (NICs), will resume from today (20).

title: Energy Minister used as a scapegoat to cover up breach of trust by the Cabinet: Joint Opposition
byline: The resignation of Power and Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody is an attempt to cover up a serious breach of collective responsibility by the Cabinet, the Joint Opposition said.

title: No disruption to construction projects despite Middle East conflict: Minister
byline: Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake has said that there is no interruption to ongoing construction projects in the country despite the prevailing conflict in the Middle East.

title: Six foreign envoys present credentials to President
byline: Two High Commissioners, three Ambassadors and an Apostolic Nuncio-designate of the Holy See presented their credentials to Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat this morning (20).

title: Three injured in Watawala three-wheeler plunge
byline: Three persons were injured when a three-wheeler carrying a family veered off the road and plunged nearly 50 feet into a ravine in the Carolina area of Watawala along the Hatton–Colombo main road on Monday (20), police said.

title: Tehran has ‘no plans to participate’ in new talks
byline: Tehran is not currently planning to take part in new talks with the US, Iran state media reported on Sunday evening, as its military accused America of violating a fragile ceasefire between the two countries, hours after Donald Trump said he was dispatching negotiators to Islamabad.

title: Major 7.4-magnitude quake hits off Japan, tsunami warning issued
byline: An earthquake ‌with a preliminary magnitude of 7.4 struck off ​the northeastern coast of ​Japan on Monday afternoon, ⁠the Japan Meteorological ​Agency said.

title: Steps to regulate boat services after Gregory Lake incident
byline: Nuwara Eliya Mayor Upali Wanigasekera says that measures will be taken to regulate boat services following an incident in which two tourist boats capsized at Gregory Lake.

title: Ex-Minister Piyasena Gamage granted bail in corruption case
byline: Former Minister of Skills Development and Vocational Training, Piyasena Gamage, who was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption over corruption charges, was today ordered to be released on bail by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.

title: Over 21,000 food establishments inspected during festive season raids: PHI
byline: A special island-wide food safety inspection programme carried out during the festive season has resulted in widespread inspections and enforcement actions, according to the Sri Lanka Public Health Inspectors Association.

title: SLPP to gear up for political comeback in New Year: MR
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa indicated that a “significant plan” is in place aimed at regaining political power in the New Year, stating that a political shift is imminent and that the party is fully prepared for it.

title: Student volunteer initiative launched at Jaffna uni
byline: A new student-led volunteer initiative aimed at strengthening community engagement and social responsibility has been launched at the University of Jaffna.

title: Japan issues rare special advisory over chance of more powerful quake
byline: Authorities have warned residents of northeastern Japan to prepare for an even larger earthquake after a magnitude 7.7 quake struck off the coast of Iwate on Monday, triggering tsunami across a broad swath of the area.

title: Trump ‘considering’ lifting naval blockade
byline: Donald Trump will consider lifting the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in order to overcome the deadlock in peace talks.

title: PCB imposes one-year PSL ban on Dasun Shanaka for contract breach
byline: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Monday announced imposing a two-year ban on Sri Lanka’s T20I captain Dasun Shanaka from participating in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) over his ’’unilateral withdrawal’’ from the ongoing 11th edition.

title: Fire at Rajasthan refinery site a day before PM Modi’s inauguration
byline: A fire broke out at the Pachpadra Refinery in Balotra on Monday afternoon — just a day before its scheduled inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

title: UNP denies social media report on May Day rally
byline: The United National Party (UNP) today denied the social media report which said the party is to hold a joint May Day rally with other parties.

title: Excise Department earns record revenue in first quarter of 2026
byline: The Sri Lanka Excise Department has earned a record revenue of Rs. 70.4 billion in the first quarter of 2026, exceeding the set revenue target of Rs. 61.95 billion for the same period.

title: Anura Karunathilaka sworn in as Energy Minister
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Anura Karunathilaka as the new Minister of Energy.

title: Philippines, US and allies start military exercises testing ’real‑world’ readiness
byline: Philippine and U.S. forces will carry out maritime strike drills on a remote Philippine ‌island near Taiwan during annual exercises that started on Monday, which Manila’s military chief said would test their readiness under ’’real‑world conditions’’.

title: Selfless Matthews drops forbidden Bombshell
byline: Newly crowned Premier League cricket champions Colts Cricket Club had to dodge many a bullet, swim past undercurrents, avoid stepping on toes and could not even voice their grievances as they trudged along to win the coveted First Class inter club title in what was their 150th year in existence away from the prying eyes.

title: Eshan Malinga bringing back art of reverse-swing
byline: Sri Lanka has most of its premier cricketers playing in either the Indian Premier League (IPL) or Pakistan Super League (PSL) at the moment and while the likes of Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka have made their mark with the bat, Eshan Malinga has made a huge impact with the ball. Malinga who unfortunately missed out on the World Cup due to injury earlier this year, has been in superb form for Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) this season.

title: PHIs warn of rat fever risk during New Year festivities
byline: Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) have warned of an increased risk of rat fever during New Year festival activities, particularly traditional folk games held near water sources and paddy fields.

title: Iran has not changed its decision to abstain from talks with US - Iranian media
byline: Despite US President Trump telling the New York Post that the US delegation is en route to Pakistan, Iran has not ’’altered its decision to abstain’’ from the talks, according to Iran’s hard-line Tasnim news agency which is affiliated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

title: Special traffic plan near Kochchikade church tomorrow
byline: A special traffic management plan will be implemented around St. Anthony’s Shrine tomorrow (April 21, 2026) to facilitate religious observances marking the seventh anniversary of the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks.

title: Philippines, US and allies start military exercises testing ’real‑world’ readiness
byline: Philippine and U.S. forces will carry out maritime strike drills on a remote Philippine ‌island near Taiwan during annual exercises that started on Monday, which Manila’s military chief said would test their readiness under ’’real‑world conditions’’.

byline: Tehran is not currently planning to take part in new talks with the US, Iran state media reported on Sunday evening, as its military accused America of violating a fragile ceasefire between the two countries, hours after Donald Trump said he was dispatching negotiators to Islamabad.

byline: An earthquake ‌with a preliminary magnitude of 7.4 struck off ​the northeastern coast of ​Japan on Monday afternoon, ⁠the Japan Meteorological ​Agency said.
